lines.text: A small kingdom of mountains and grasslands, and the last absolute monarchy in Africa. This is the story of Eswatini.
In the eighteen hundreds, King Mswati the Second made the Swazi a strong nation, and his people took their name from him.
Sobhuza the Second became king as a baby in 1899, and reigned for eighty-two years, one of the longest reigns ever recorded.
Under British rule, the town of Mbabane grew around the administration, and became the capital.
In 1961, Mlilwane became the country's first protected area for wildlife.
A few years later came Hlane Royal National Park, the largest protected area in the kingdom.
In 1968 a prince was born who, as Mswati the Third, would be king from 1986, an absolute monarch.
That same year, Swaziland became independent from Britain. In 2018 it took the name Eswatini.
In 2021, people took to the streets to demand democracy, and the protests were put down by force.
From Mswati the Second to Mswati the Third, the Swazi kings still rule.
